# Format as rename-as.tsv: old, new, kind, where, comment; whole-word rows for src/tools/rename-table.py.
# Kinds: file (path rows), type, function (file-scope, static or not; ",public" when declared in src/include/vir/),
#   constant (enumerators and constant macros), macro (function-like), variable, field, unsafe (commented out).
# Prefixes: vir_ for src/vir/, virbuild_ for the builder and vectorizer in src/codegen/vir/, a64_vir_ / x64_vir_ for the
#   lowerings (STYLE: a target's code in a shared module carries both).  Constants: VIR_, VIRBUILD_, A64_VIR_.
#   - the text form: opcode, type and condition spellings ("add", "i32", "slt", ...: strings of vir/table.c), pass names of
#     VCC_VIR_PASSES, .vir files and test expectations under src/test/vir*.  The enumerators behind them (VO_ADD) are C
#     identifiers and do move (VIR_OP_ADD), their suffix being the opcode's spelling.
#   - names produced by the walker's second instantiation: WK_PREFIX/LO_PREFIX paste "vw_" in front of every walker function
#     and of every LO(name) (codegen/walk/prefix.h, gen-walkprefix.py).  The row `vw_` below renames the prefix itself (the
#     two #define lines of each builder file and the vw_##name of VW_NO); wk_X then becomes virbuild_<walker's new name>
#     with the walker's own table.  The suffix of an LO(X) implementation is the walker's lowering vocabulary shared by
#     x64, arm64 and VIR: rows of kind function marked "LO(X)" move the prefix only; X is renamed with codegen/walk/.
#   - already right: vir_alloc, vir_verify, vir_canon, vir_parse, vir_slot_add, vir_unit_init/alloc/free, vir_loops_build,
# SPEC-vir.md and PLAN-vir.md use many of the old names (vir_ins, vir_blk, vir_fn, vir_cfg, vir_dom, vir_uses, VO_*, ...): doc/ is
# outside the script's scope; apply with --also doc/SPEC-vir.md (the spec follows the code) once the owner agrees.
# Files not renamed: vir/vir.c is the construction API, the constant table, the CFG and dominators, canon and the unit: more than one
# job (STYLE: one job per file), a split rather than a rename; see the PR's open questions.

# rows: their meaning is documented per sweep inside alloc.c and the names should be chosen when that file is split.
# Rows of kind unsafe are commented out: the old word is also used for other things (locals, other modules), so whole-word
